date.label: Undated biblical wilderness narrative and legislation
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The received Numbers narrative contains the Israel Organized at Sinai material across Numbers 1–4.
claims.evidence: Numbers 1–4; biblical-text description, not independent evidence for an event date.

claims.claim: The exact archaeological or external historical setting of this entire passage has not been independently established.
claims.evidence: Phase 2 Dossier 1 (numbers-phase2.md): the Masoretic totals (603,550 at Num 1:46; 601,730 at Num 26:51) are Established as text, but their demographic historicity is Unknown/Debated; Adair 2025, read in full (QA Phase 4 §5.1), finds the figures more plausibly artificial literary numbers, and no primary ANE census document was inspected (source-adair-numbers-census).

claims.claim: Comparisons with related biblical laws and retellings need to preserve differences in wording, chronology, or institutional setting.
claims.evidence: Internal textual comparisons documented in CONNECTION-AUDIT.md; interpretation of literary relationship, not an archaeological observation.

connections.note: Second census contrasts the wilderness generations; its final aggregate differs.
Firstborn consecration provides a legal and theological backdrop.
Service age differs from the transport muster in Numbers 4.
Census ransom law: every man numbered from twenty years old gives half a shekel; a legal parallel, not the same census scene.
Tribal portions arranged around the sacred allotment, with city gates named for the tribes; a thematic parallel to the camp arrangement, not a retelling of Numbers 2.
Levite cleansing and consecration as substitutes for the firstborn; develops the substitution of Numbers 3.
Third age datum: Levites numbered from twenty years old and above under David; differs from the thirty-to-fifty transport muster in Numbers 4.
